Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

DelphiR 0.1.0

First release.

Data import and validation

  • delphi_template() creates an empty Excel or CSV file in the DelphiR format, with instructions and the code needed to import it.
  • delphi_data() and read_delphi() import ratings in the DelphiR wide layout, with one row per expert and one column per item, from data frames and from CSV, TSV and Excel files. Separators and decimal commas are detected automatically, and ratings are validated against the rating scale of each indicator.
  • delphi_data_long() and read_delphi(layout = "long") import ratings in long format, with one row per rating.
  • read_delphi(header_rows = 2) reads survey exports in which the first header row gives the indicators and the second the item statements. Items are coded E1, E2, … and their statements are stored as labels.
  • Rows without an expert identifier, such as summary rows with medians or quartiles, are ignored with a warning.
  • linked = FALSE declares that expert identifiers do not denote the same person across rounds, as when each round is collected with a separate questionnaire. Retention is then not computed, and stability is assessed by comparing the rounds as independent samples.
  • delphi_bind() combines tables referring to different rounds or indicators, and delphi_wide() and as.data.frame() return the ratings in wide or long format.
  • Example dataset delphi_example.

Analysis

  • delphi_describe() computes descriptive statistics by item, round and indicator, including the relative IQR, and delphi_panel() reports panel participation and retention.
  • delphi_consensus() applies the IQR consensus criterion, with an IQR of at most 20% of the rating scale by default (von der Gracht, 2012).
  • delphi_stability() assesses stability between consecutive rounds with the Wilcoxon test (the default: signed-rank for linked experts, rank-sum otherwise), with a net-change criterion based on Scheibe, Skutsch and Schofer (1975), or with both.
  • delphi_status() combines consensus and stability into four categories (consensus, unstable consensus, stable dissent and open) and identifies the items to be submitted to a further round.
  • summary() provides an overview of the panel and of the median and IQR of each item by round.

Figures and reports

  • delphi_plot_distribution(), delphi_plot_trend(), delphi_plot_consensus() and delphi_plot_map(), also available through plot(), draw publication-quality figures with ggplot2. theme_delphi() provides the common theme.
  • delphi_report() generates a self-contained round report in HTML or Word format.
  • The vignette “Introduction to DelphiR” describes the complete workflow.
